messages:
alex: heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak (prefer fused-attn when latency delta < 5ms) we're seeing steady batch growth + pad blowup on a few repros. noticed 3 OOMs on nightly perf job.

maria: can you paste the log sample?

alex: here, trimmed: ```
[2024-03-30T02:12:11Z] job=nightly shard=2 batch=34 total_seqs=128 avg_seq=342 pad_mean=768 pad_waste=1.9GB OOM at alloc workspace 4.2GB
```

alex: low-level cause looks like fused-kernel allocs requiring larger per-request workspace. when batch grows (continuous batching) padding weight multiplies the per-seq workspace, so small delta -> big mem blowup.

tariq: hmm. is the growth from model-side seq-length inflation (KV cache replays) or scheduler packing?

alex: a mix. KV cache replaying prefixes increases active sequence lengths on warm caches, scheduler then packs more because latency looked fine, so the continuous batching window stretches. packer + fused kernel => oversized workspace per request.

jen: any quick telemetry to confirm kernel variant vs workspace size correlation?

alex: added a short profiler patch that logs kernel_name + workspace_alloc. sample snippet: ```python
# in allocator tracepoint
print(f"{kernel_name} workspace={bytes_alloc/1024**2:.1f}MB seq_len={seq_len} batch={batch_size}")
```
collected 200 lines: fused-attn entries are ~28% larger workspace on median seq_len 320.

ciara: that matches what I saw in perf-bot flame: fused kernel moves buffers earlier into GPU memory and pins larger temp tensors. perf-bot do you have the flame link?

perf-bot: https://perf.internal/runs/2024-03-30/7891 — flame shows 25% more scratch for fused-attn path. :mag_right:

maria: proposal: revert aggressive preference; instead do sampling-driven selection i.e. choose kernel per-slice based on expected padded-workspace cost. sampling = take N batches, estimate pad waste by seq length distribution, pick kernel that minimizes (latency + alpha * expected_mem). alpha tuned by SLA.

tariq: +1. also we should stop continuous-batcher from unboundedly growing if per-request workspace crosses soft cap. put an adaptive cap: when expected padding * workspace_per_seq > workspace_soft_limit, limit batch growth and prioritize smaller batches.

alex: sketch of pad estimator I hacked: ```python
def expected_pad_cost(seq_hist, bucket_edges, workspace_per_seq):
    # seq_hist: counts per seq length bucket
    expected_pad = 0
    for L,count in seq_hist.items():
        padded = next_bucket_size(L) - L
        expected_pad += padded * count
    return expected_pad * workspace_per_seq
```
This gives a quick ranking for kernel variants.

jen: could we do a cheap online sampler (1% of requests) to keep distribution fresh? avoids stale estimates when KV cache warms up.

ciara: also consider allocator-level reuse across kernel variants: if fused needs bigger scratch, try to reuse non-fused scratch buffers or maintain small pool of "oversize" buffers to avoid fragmentation spikes.

alex: actionable plan: 1) add 1% sampler telemetry + estimator, 2) patch continuous-batcher to enforce soft-workspace cap and backpressure, 3) add micro-pool for oversize scratch reuse, 4) canary-revert kernel pref tweak if telemetry shows >10% pad increase.

maria: timeline?

alex: I can do (1) and (2) in a single PR today, (3) needs allocator touches — targ Wed, (4) immediate rollback if nightly crosses threshold.

tariq: put a metric: pad_waste_bytes_per_batch and pad_waste_rate, alert if > X for 30m.

perf-bot: created perf alert ticket #PI-612 with a runbook: https://internal/tickets/PI-612 :white_check_mark:

jen: assign owners? alex for sampler+batcher, tariq for soft caps and metrics, ciara for allocator pool review, maria to coordinate canary.

alex: noted. I'll open draft PR with profiler logs attached and a short doc on estimator math.

ciara: FYI — I'll prototype a 2-size oversize pool (1.25x, 1.5x) and measure reuse hit rate before merging.

maria: thanks all. if anyone reproduces an OOM, drop logs here + the kernel trace line. :heart:

alex: will do.
